subject: QuickCart deployment fit and next steps — capacity follow-up
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@quickcart.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: QuickCart deployment fit and next steps — capacity follow-up

Samir, great to meet you on the call this morning — thanks for walking us through the checkout flow and the latency pain. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can recommend the most cost-effective deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC).

Key notes from the demo:
- Primary endpoint: personalized recommendations + fraud scoring combined in a single request.
- Typical request length: ~60 tokens average; 99th percentile bursts can include expanded context up to ~320 tokens.
- Peak observed demo QPS looked ~80–110 in your traffic simulator.
- Critical SLA: p95 latency target around 150ms for human-discount checkout flows.

Questions we need to finalize recommendation:
1) Can you confirm peak sustained QPS (15min window) and absolute peak burst QPS?
2) What percent of traffic requires the full 320-token context vs short (<=64 tokens)?
3) Any regulatory requirement (VPC/KMS/SOC2) we should plan for during pilot?

Initial shading: from what we saw, your latency target plus burstiness makes Dedicated capacity attractive for predictable p95 guarantees, but Hosted with careful batching/caching could be fine for an initial rollout if bursts are moderate and you accept some fallback behavior.

Next steps I propose:
- You share the QPS breakdown and token-size distribution (CSV or quick summary) — Connor can run a cost/latency simulation.
- We put together a short pilot proposal (2-week perf pilot) that can run on Dedicated capacity with autoscale margins configured to 2x observed peak.
- If you need SOC2/KMS now, we’ll map to Private deployment options in parallel.

Attachments: post-demo-capacity-notes.pdf (short call notes).

Available for a 30-min follow-up Thursday afternoon — does 3pm PT work?

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: post-demo-capacity-notes.pdf]
From: Samir Patel <samir@quickcart.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@quickcart.com>
Date: 2028-05-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuickCart deployment fit and next steps — capacity follow-up

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the clear note. Answers below and a couple of clarifications: 

1) Peak sustained (15m window): 120 qps. Absolute peak bursts (1–2 min): 220 qps (we see these during promo pushes).
2) Token distribution: ~80% of calls are small (<=64 tokens). ~18% are medium (65–160), ~2% are long (160–320). The long ones are usually when we pull enriched user history.
3) Compliance: SOC2 in process; target completion Q4. For now we need encryption-at-rest + key management (we use AWS KMS). Private on-prem is not required at this stage.

Follow-up question: if we start on Hosted, can we rely on automatic fallback to Hosted for bursts if Dedicated is mis-sized? Ideally we want a hybrid: Dedicated for steady low-latency, Hosted for overflow. Any pitfalls?

Also attaching a quick sample traffic dump (small csv) — let me know if you need anything else.

Thanks,
Samir
CTO, QuickCart
[attachment: quickcart-traffic-sample.csv]
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@quickcart.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuickCart deployment fit and next steps — capacity follow-up

Samir — perfect, this is very helpful. Based on the numbers you shared (120 qps sustained, 220 qps short bursts, p95 target 150ms, 80% short requests) here’s our recommended path and rationale: 

Recommendation (short): Dedicated reserved capacity for the production rollout + Hosted overflow/fallback for rare bursts.

Why Dedicated first:
- Predictable p95: Dedicated lets us provision GPU pools sized to meet the 150ms p95 with predictable queuing characteristics.
- Efficient handling of mixed token lengths: we can tune batching windows and KV cache sizing on the Dedicated pool to keep latency tight for the 80% short calls while servicing longer contexts without blowing up cost.
- Cost predictability: at your sustained 120 qps profile, Dedicated is typically 20–35% cheaper per token compared to pure Hosted at scale, especially once KV caching reduces repeated prefix compute.

Why keep Hosted overflow:
- Bursts to ~220 qps: we can configure smart routing to spill overflow to Redwood Hosted to avoid request failures; fallback adds marginal latency but prevents dropped requests during promos.
- Operational simplicity for early rollouts: we’ll own the overflow routing and you don’t need to pre-commit capacity for 1–2 minute spikes.

Pilot plan (2 weeks):
1) Week 0: Provision a Dedicated GPU pool sized at ~1.8x your sustained qps (estimate attached calculations).
2) Week 1: Synthetic load test + live shadow traffic on 10% of production. Measure p50/p95/p99 and adjust batching/latency buckets.
3) Week 2: Gradual rollout to 50% traffic with Hosted overflow enabled; run the safety rollback plan.

Deliverables and asks from QuickCart:
- Full 24h traffic CSV (Connor will ingest and produce the latency/cost sims).
- Confirm AWS KMS key usage model so we can scope encryption-in-transit and at-rest endpoints.
- Sign-off on pilot SLOs (I’ll attach a one-pager to the HubSpot deal).

Estimated timeline:
- Pilot kickoff as soon as we get the traffic CSV + KMS details — we can start provisioning within 3 business days.
- Pilot completion in ~2 weeks, then decision for reserved capacity commit.

Attached: capacity-proposal-quickcart.pdf and latency-qps-calcs.xlsx (high-level sizing calc). I’ll open a HubSpot task and a shared Drive folder with the pilot artifacts.

Proposed next call: Friday 1pm PT to review Connor’s sims and finalize pilot SLOs. Does that work for you?

Thanks — looping Connor and Marissa to flag any operational caveats.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0123 | aisha@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference
[Attachments: capacity-proposal-quickcart.pdf, latency-qps-calcs.xlsx]
